title: Developer Urban Splash forced to pay £45m over Manchester fire safety works

input.summary: A tribunal rules public money spent on safety work at seven blocks in Manchester should be repaid
input.evidence_text: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. input.lead: Sutton Community Fridge aims to reduce food waste and to help people who are struggling financially

input.evidence_text: A small food shed set up on a driveway in Cheshire less than two years ago has grown into a community hub which helps about 200 people each week Sutton Community Fridge was set up in December 2024 by Gayle Parks to tackle food waste and help families in the Macclesfield area access affordable food The project collects surplus stock from supermarkets, charities and businesses that would otherwise be thrown away and makes it available to buy at a low price The idea came to Gayle after about £15,000 worth of stock was stolen during a burglary at her family's pet shop In the aftermath, she relied on apps offering surplus food to help feed her own family She said: ''It made me question how could perfectly good food be going to waste when families were struggling to put food on their tables?''

title: Man hit by bus in Stockport missed granddaughter's birth by a day

input.lead: Ross Grealey's children said their father was "one of a kind" and loved by many
input.summary: Ross Grealey's children said their father was "one of a kind" and loved by many
input.evidence_text: Man hit by bus in Stockport missed granddaughter's birth by a day - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Carla Grealey said her father Ross was "one of a kind" and loved by many By Haider Saleem North West Published 5 November 2026 The family of a man who died after being hit by a bus in Greater Manchester said they were heartbroken he missed the birth of his granddaughter by just one day. Ross Grealey died after he was struck near Winifred Road in Stockport on 30 October, Greater Manchester Police said. His son, who is also called Ross, said a baby girl was born the following day and wished his father had been able to meet her. His daughter Carla Grealey described her father as "one of a kind" and said he was loved by many. In a tribute his son said: "You're now a grandad to a beautiful baby girl, who was born just a day after this tragedy. I wish with all my heart that you could have met her." "A little piece of you will live on through her," he said. Carla added: "I'm truly heartbroken. I still can't understand any of it. I just wish it hadn't happened." Staff at The Wellspring, who supported Grealey, said he was always ready with a story, a smile and a hug. "He made our world a better place simply by being in it," the team said. title: Pat Karney funeral: Andy Burnham says he shaped Manchester

input.lead: Burnham recalls the politician's humour as Manchester mourns the man behind its celebrations
input.summary: Burnham recalls the politician's humour as Manchester mourns the man behind its celebrations
input.evidence_text: Pat Karney funeral: Andy Burnham says he shaped Manchester - BBC News Image caption, Prime Minister Andy Burnham joined mourners at St Mary's Roman Catholic Church to pay his respects to Pat Karney By Richard Stead , Kaya Black , Reporting from Manchester and Haider Saleem , North West Published 5 November 2026 Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described long-serving Manchester councillor Pat Karney as a "political genius" at his funeral, saying his "spirit is in every street" of the city. Burnham, who worked alongside the Labour politician for 25 years, told mourners: "I loved Pat and I looked up to him and I will miss him as we all will." Karney, who represented Harpurhey in north Manchester from 1979, died on 13 October aged 78 . He was known for championing the city's major celebrations and played a significant role in its political life. Before the service, his hearse paused in Albert Square, where a Ferris wheel displayed the message "Thank You Pat" beside the city's Christmas Markets. During his funeral address, Burnham recalled the many sides of Karney, from his political campaigning to his sense of humour and love of celebrations. title: Man catches thief with Apple AirTag hidden in stone

input.lead: Matt Smith hid the tracker inside a piece of stone and police followed the trail to the culprit's house
input.summary: Matt Smith hid the tracker inside a piece of stone and police followed the trail to the culprit's house
input.evidence_text: Man catches thief with Apple AirTag hidden in stone - BBC News Image caption, Matt Smith says people were "miffed" with stones being taken so he had to take action By Emma Stanley North West Published 5 November 2026 A thief who was stealing a wall piece by piece was caught when a man put a tracking device in one of the stones. Matt Smith said people living near Rufford Old Hall in Lancashire, "were getting a bit miffed" with stones being taken from the 300-year-old boundary wall. So he put an Apple AirTag - a coin-sized tracking device people attach to keys or wallets in case they lose them - inside one of the stones. Police followed the trail to an address in Wigan, and earlier this month, a man pleaded guilty at Wigan Magistrates' Court to two counts of theft and one count of handling stolen goods. Last October, about 30 stones went missing from a half-mile-long stretch of road which connects Holmeswood and Rufford. "We looked at installing some CCTV, but it costs and with the wall being attacked at random places at random times, in a half mile stretch of wall, it was going to be hard to cover that area," Smith, a parish councillor, told BBC Radio Lancashire. Image source, Lancashire Police Image caption, About 30 stones had gone missing from along a half-mile-long stretch of road which connects Holmeswood and Rufford He added: "So we put some lovely 'smile you're on camera' signs up and unfortunately that didn't deter them. "We'd noticed it was the smaller of the stones that were being taken, so we put a tracking device in what we thought would maybe be the next stone to be taken. input.summary: Transport for Greater Manchester confirms it has no plans to implement a congestion charge in the
input.evidence_text: Transport bosses in Greater Manchester have confirmed there are no plans for a congestion charge in the city centre Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed plans to "invest heavily" in public transport instead of introducing a congestion charge, the Local Democracy Reporting Service reported The transport agency said it will be investing invest £2.5bn of government money into the region between 2027 and 2032, and bringing trains to the Bee Network from December A report published by Manchester City Council on Tuesday revealed traffic had become so bad that it had cost the region's economy billions of pounds "There are no plans for a congestion charge in any part of Greater Manchester, instead we are investing heavily in the Bee Network to give people a reliable alternative to getting in their car," a TfGM spokesperson said "One tram full of people could replace around 200 cars on the road and a double decker bus around 75, demonstrating the benefits of getting more people on board the Bee Network."

title: Landlady says up to 60 teenagers attacked pub with fireworks

input.lead: Paula says she had to lock her customers in for hours as the gang aimed fireworks at the pub
input.summary: Paula says she had to lock her customers in for hours as the gang aimed fireworks at the pub
input.evidence_text: A landlady said she locked customers inside her pub for hours while a group of teenagers attacked it with fireworks Salford pub manager Paula, 61, said she and 30 customers hid out as "about 60 teenagers" bombarded The Plough, in Cadishead, on Saturday Police were called, and footage from the incident, appearing to show doors being kicked and a bus driver being assaulted, has since been shared on social media "It was very scary. "But more starting coming and then there was 60 of them."

input.evidence_text: The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
